title: H-16
summary: 16mm camera taking 100ft (30m) and 50ft (15m) daylight loading spools, with automatic threading and loop forming, a constant-speed spring motor, and a rotating turret accommodating three interchangeable C-mount lenses.

title: H-16 Supreme
summary: 16mm camera with 100ft (30m) and 50ft (15m) daylight loading spool capacity.

title: H-16 S
summary: Non-reflex, turret-style 16mm camera.

title: H-16 M
summary: Accommodates a single interchangeable C-mount lens; variable speeds of 8, 16, 24, 32 and 64 frames per second.

title: H-16 M-4
summary: Began production in 1965.

title: H-16 M-5
summary: Began production in 1967.

title: H-16 Reflex
summary: Rotating turret with three interchangeable RX-type C-mount lenses; reflex viewing through a semi-reflecting prism with groundglass focusing.

title: H-16 REX
summary: Introduced in 1959.

title: H-16 REX-5
summary: Began production in 1966; introduced in 1967.

title: H-8
summary: Double 8mm model of the H camera line, introduced 1938.

title: H-8 REX
summary: The first 8mm reflex camera manufactured by Bolex.

title: L-8 (early model)
summary: Double 8mm camera introduced in 1942.

title: B-8
summary: Double 8mm camera introduced in 1953.

title: B-8L
summary: First in the series of "Compumatic" cameras, providing an easy method for determining proper exposure using a photo-electric selenium cell and galvanometer needle.

title: C-8
summary: Double 8mm camera introduced in 1954.

title: 150 Super
summary: The first Bolex Super 8 model. Unconventional design with a built-in lens, bright reflex viewfinder, and a film chamber located on top of the camera body.

title: 155 Macrozoom
summary: Improved on the 150 Super. The Macrozoom lens focuses as close as one inch; the viewing system features a coincident-image rangefinder.

title: 160 Macrozoom
summary: Introduced in 1970, the latest model in the Macrozoom series.

title: 7.5 Macrozoom
summary: Introduced in 1969 as a lower-priced option to the 155/160 series.

title: S1 Automatic
summary: Assigned its own unique serial number range by Paillard in 1963 alongside the P-series and K-series cameras.

title: Model G
summary: Introduced in 1936 in "monofilm" and "multifilm" models; the multifilm included a tool-free parts kit of reel spindles, sprockets, gate and guide-rollers to adapt the projector to various film gauges.
Projected 8mm film at fixed speeds of 18 and 5 frames per second forward, and 18 fps in reverse.

title: M-8
summary: Designed to run off a mains power supply of 110–125 Volts.

title: SM 8
summary: Magnetic sound projection and recording, with a built-in 2W / 15 Ohm speaker.

title: S-221
summary: Plays back silent or sound film with optical or magnetic tracks, and records sound onto 16mm magnetic-striped film.

title: Kern-Paillard
summary: Kern lenses of Aarau, Switzerland were the premier optics supplied for Bolex cameras across the 1940s, 1950s and 1960s, including the RX series computed for the reflex prism of the H-16 Reflex cameras.

title: Hugo Meyer
summary: Pre-war Bolex cameras were often equipped with Hugo Meyer lenses, a German manufacturer of photographic lenses founded in the late 1800s.

title: C.P. Goerz
summary: Founded in 1886 by Carl Paul Goerz in Berlin. The Goerz Kino-Hypar was an air-spaced, three-element motion picture lens used by both professional and amateur cinematographers.

title: Wollensak
summary: Established in 1899 in Rochester, NY. Good quality construction priced much lower than Kern lenses; a popular choice with amateurs throughout the 1940s and 1950s.

title: SOM Berthiot
summary: Société d'Optique et de Mécanique Berthiot produced C- and D-mount motion picture lenses for professional and amateur use, as well as the Pan Cinor series of zoom lenses.

title: Angénieux
summary: Documented on the original lens index alongside Kern-Paillard, Hugo Meyer, Goerz, Wollensak and SOM Berthiot; dedicated pages pending recovery.

title: Filters and Lens Accessories
summary: Filters and lens accessories by decade.

title: Viewfinders
summary: Viewfinders and viewing accessories by decade.

title: Motors
summary: Electric drive and sync motors. The first sound-synchronous motor for Bolex cameras was manufactured in 1965 by Perfectone of Bienne, Switzerland.

title: Cases
summary: Carrying cases, including the Bolex Aluminum Carrying Case — "strong enough to stand on" — sized for an H camera with zoom lens, Matte Box and Unimotor attached.

title: Tripods and Grips
summary: Includes the Reporter Grip (1962) for H-model cameras with quick-set base attachment and fingertip release; the Declic H grip for flat-base H models; and an 11 oz monopod introduced in 1961 for the B, C and D models.

title: Matte Box
summary: Introduced in 1962 for any H camera; produced effects with masks and served as filter holder and lens shade. Dedicated page pending recovery.

title: Editing Equipment
summary: Editing equipment by decade.

title: Miscellaneous
summary: Aftermarket items and modifications alongside Paillard-manufactured accessories.
